evidence.text: Unit of measure for farm 田 land 土

A village (里) is an area of land (土) where people have fields (田). In simplified Chinese 里 is also used to mean "inside", while in traditional Chinese this meaning is written with a separate character 裡.
居也。从田从土。凡里之屬皆从里。

Ideogrammic compound (會意 /会意): 田 (“field”) + 土 (“soil; earth”) – a measure of land and fields; mile; place.
From Proto-Sino-Tibetan *rwəʔ (“village”) (STEDT, under PTB *r/g-wa). Cognate with 丘 (OC *kʰʷɯ) "hill, mound" & 街 (OC *kreː, *kreː) "road crossing, street"; outsides Sinitic, cognate with Mizo khua (“village”), Lai khûa (“village, cosmos”), Burmese ရွာ (rwa, “village”); Schuessler (2007) also proposes cognacy with Tibetan ར་བ (ra ba, “fence, enclosure, wall, pen”) by pointing to a semantic parallel between English town and German Zaun (“fence”).
Alternatively, possibly related to 理 (lǐ) "to divide into equal sections", yet Schuessler also noted that early Chinese villages were not systematically planned and platted.
居也。从田从土。凡里之屬皆从里。

evidence.field: 形義通解; 里字形、讀音與早期用例
evidence.text: This dictionary states 里 first appears in Western Zhou bronze inscriptions, formed from 田 and 土 and interpreted as a place where land and fields are habitable. It reports later bronze forms where strokes in 田 and 土 run together, with the stroke in 土 later extended into the seal-script shape. It cites bronze uses for a settlement head (令方彝), a distance measure (中山王鼎), and as a writing for 裏 in a garment-lining phrase (伯䢅鼎). It also cites Warring States Qin slips for settlement and distance-measure uses, and a Guodian slip where 里 writes 理. These are the dictionary's reported readings of cited artifacts; I did not inspect the glyph images or artifact editions independently.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 里

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 釋義; variant relation
evidence.text: The Ministry entry gives the Shuowen account 居也。从田，从土 and glosses 里 as habitation, neighborhood/lane, native place, administrative unit, interior (通裡), distance unit, and surname. Its citation sequence includes the received Shijing line 將仲子兮，無踰我里 for a settlement and Shijing 百里 for a distance expression; those literary citation dates do not by themselves establish when each sense first arose. The entry points to 裡 as a variant for the interior sense.
evidence.title: A04256 里 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.field: 《說文》; 形義通解; 金文與詞義
evidence.text: The entry for 裏 gives Xu Shen's analysis 衣內也。从衣，里聲 and reports Western Zhou bronze evidence. It cites the Shijing 綠衣黄裏 for garment lining and a bronze vessel inscription 彔伯簋 with 虎冪朱裏, where 裏 denotes the inside layer of a chariot cover. It says the sense broadened from a lining/interior layer to general 'inside'; the page does not establish a precise date for that semantic extension. It identifies 裡 as an alternative character form, not as the source of 裏.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 裏

evidence.field: 裏字音系資料; 《廣韻》; 形義通解
evidence.text: The page records 裏 as 良士切 in Guangyun, Middle Chinese category 來開三之上, and reports that the graph is a phonosemantic compound with 衣 as semantic element and 里 as phonetic. This supports the historical source's phonetic analysis; it is not an independent reconstruction of the pronunciation of the original referent of 里.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 裏

evidence.field: 異體字; Unicode codepoint and reading display
evidence.text: The entry identifies 裡 as U+88E1 and says it is the same character as 裏; its Shuowen panel displays the 裏 explanation 衣內也。从衣，里聲. The page characterizes 裡 as a later form/variant in the account for 裏. Because the page does not specify that 裡 is a standardized simplified counterpart, this evidence supports a variant-form relation, not simplified_form.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 裡

evidence.field: 形義通解; bronze and manuscript attestations
evidence.text: The entry says 里 first appears in Western Zhou bronze inscriptions and analyzes it as 田 plus 土, interpreted as land suitable for habitation. It reports that strokes in the two elements run together in bronze forms, and that a dot in 土 was extended into a short stroke in later forms underlying seal script. It cites bronze uses for a settlement head (令方彝), a distance measure (中山王鼎), and writing 裏 in a phrase on 伯䢅鼎; Warring States Qin slips use it for settlements and distance, and a Guodian slip uses it for 理. These are the dictionary’s reports of artifact readings, not my independent inspection of the artifacts.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 里

evidence.field: 《說文》; 形義通解; historical reading
evidence.text: The page gives the Shuowen account 居也。从田从土 and identifies 田 and 土 as the graph’s components. It records 里 as 良士切 in Guangyun, Middle Chinese category 來開三之上. The Middle Chinese data do not establish the earliest pronunciation of the graph or independently date a word sense.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 里

evidence.field: 《說文》; 形義通解; bronze and received-text uses
evidence.text: The page reports that 裏 is a bronze-era phonosemantic graph with 衣 as semantic element and 里 as phonetic. It gives the Shuowen statement 衣内也。从衣，里聲 and Guangyun 來開三之上. It cites the Shijing 綠衣黃裏 for a garment lining, and 彔伯簋 虎冪朱裏 for the lining of a chariot cover; it describes a broader ‘inside’ sense as an extension but does not date when it arose. Its analysis supports 里’s phonetic role in 裏, independently of the uncertain original referent or earliest pronunciation of 里.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 裏

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: The official Unicode GetUnihanData pages for all three characters returned internal errors, so exact kMandarin values remain unverified externally in this run; no local repository row was available through the web tool.

The CUHK dictionary summarizes inscription and manuscript evidence with cited artifact names and line references, but the ancient glyph images and primary artifact editions were not independently inspected. Do not claim direct visual paleographic inspection.

For 里, Shuowen's analysis is historically important but is not by itself confirmation of how the graph originated; the dossier's mnemonically phrased 'farm land and soil' gloss should be distinguished from CUHK's account and caveat that the semantic explanation is interpretation.

The inscriptional instance where 里 writes 裏 is graphic borrowing/loan use of the whole graph in context, distinct from 里's phonetic role as a component in 裏. The early sound relationship is asserted by Shuowen and the dictionary, but the original referent and earliest pronunciation of the graph 里 are not established here.

No dated first occurrence for the distance-unit sense or for general 'inside' as a word is established. Bronze and Warring States sources provide attestations, not a complete semantic chronology; received Shijing lines cannot alone date a sense's origin.
No exact Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese comparison for 里 and 裏 was verified against the required local TSV. Avoid merging the dossier's distinct * (mə.)rəʔ, *m.rəʔ, and Zhengzhang *rɯʔ notations.

No external evidence inspected establishes that the village word 里 is cognate with Proto-Sino-Tibetan or the proposed Tibeto-Burman forms in dossier E4; those claims remain unverified and should not be used as graphic-origin evidence.
The source corpus repeatedly references CUHK dictionary data, but reuse terms for a versioned local extract were not verified; do not recommend or create a bulk extract on this evidence.

The repository’s supplied Xiaoxuetang query candidates were not included in this invocation. External search surfaced one image record, but its source label is 庫, so no Xiaoxuetang glyph candidate is selected.

The candidate selected is a modern vector redraw of an ancient-script form, not an artifact photograph. The actual original image endpoint could not be opened by the web tool because it rejected the SVG content type; the Commons provenance and rights page was inspected.
The ancient artifact images and primary editions cited by CUHK were not independently examined. Dates and early uses here are reported from that dictionary’s summaries.

The distance-unit and general interior word senses have attestations cited by the dictionary, but their first emergence and semantic links are not established. The graph use of 里 for 裏 is distinct from the phonetic component role of 里 within 裏.

No independently supported name or original pronunciation for the depicted referent of 里 was located or needed to support its role as 裏’s phonetic component. No exact Baxter–Sagart comparison is asserted.
The CUHK corpus’s bulk reuse terms were not verified; retain concise character-specific citations rather than creating a local extract.
